payout_quote: On Scripted, you can either claim jobs from clients you match with or submit pitches for projects that appeal to you. Posted jobs already have a set rate, which is clearly displayed. With pitching, you can set your own rate.
steps: Fill out the Scripted writer registration form and pass the writing skills test.
Submit a writing sample and apply to your specialties (you only see jobs in accepted specialties).
Wait for application review (can take up to two weeks); apply to several specialties at once.
Once accepted, claim SmartMatch jobs instantly or browse Blog Ideas and pitch clients with your price, word count, and outline.
Complete accepted work; posted jobs show the set rate up front.
catches: Selective: application review can take up to two weeks and not all specialties are approved.
Pitched projects are not guaranteed — clients may ignore or reject your pitch.
Claimed SmartMatch jobs go fast; competition for instant-claim work is real.
You only see jobs in your approved specialties, limiting breadth.
Income depends on winning pitches and claiming jobs; nothing is promised.
biggest_catch: Acceptance is selective and pitched work is never guaranteed: you can spend weeks getting in and still earn nothing if no client accepts your pitches.
eligibility: Writers who can pass the skills test and get specialties approved.
timing: Jobs post continuously; application review up to two weeks.

c1.evidence: Scripted's own site states the mechanism: 'On Scripted, you can either claim jobs from clients you match with or submit pitches for projects that appeal to you. Posted jobs already have a set rate, which is clearly displayed. With pitching, you can set your own rate.'

c2.evidence: Official terms publish no fixed payout range — rates are per job or self-set per pitch; framed as variable.

c3.evidence: Steps follow the official flow: registration, skills test, sample, specialty application, review, claim/pitch.

c4.evidence: Applying and using the platform are free for writers; no upfront fee documented.

s1.note: Eligibility is writers who pass the test and specialty review.
